issues.description: In the solution for Aufgabe 08 the FROM clause lists the table Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde, but the WHERE clause references Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.gemeindeschluessel. This creates an invalid/mismatched SQL query (reference to a table not present in FROM) and contradicts the problem statement which asks for counting Radwegen related to Gemeinden with PLZ > 96400.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the table reference so the same table is used consistently. For example, change the FROM clause to use Radweg_zu_Gemeinde: "FROM Gemeinde, Radweg_zu_Gemeinde" and keep the WHERE condition "WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.gemeindeschluessel AND Gemeinde.plz > 96400". Alternatively, if Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde was intended, update the WHERE to reference Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde instead and ensure the task text matches the table used.

issues.description: The solution SQL for Aufgabe 08 inconsistently references two different table identifiers for the same conceptual entity: the FROM clause uses Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde while the WHERE clause uses Radweg_zu_Gemeinde. The problem statement asks for Radwegen (Radweg_zu_Gemeinde). This mismatch will confuse students about which table to use and makes the provided solution incorrect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the table identifier consistent with the problem intent (Radwege). In aufgabe08.sql replace Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde in the FROM clause with Radweg_zu_Gemeinde so the query reads e.g. FROM Gemeinde, Radweg_zu_Gemeinde WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.gemeindeschluessel AND Gemeinde.plz > 96400.
